### F1 (BLOCKING) Canonicalization silently collapses distinct contents, breaking "content change flips hash"

Spec passage violated (REQ-CP-05 scenario 1): "Given an item whose content changes in any way, when the bundle rebuilds, then its itemRevision hash changes while its item ID does not."
Contract clause violated: "canonical-JSON sorted-keys SHA-256" -- the serializer does not produce canonical JSON for non-plain values and never rejects them.

Empirical results (node --experimental-strip-types probe, importing computeItemRevision):

- NaN===null? true; Infinity===null? true; NaN===Infinity? true
  JSON.stringify(NaN) and JSON.stringify(Infinity) both yield the string null, so a content edit changing a numeric field from NaN or Infinity to literal null (or between NaN and Infinity) does NOT change the hash. Distinct contents, identical revision. Direct scenario-1 violation.
- Date===emptyObj? true; Map===emptyObj? true; Set===emptyObj? true
  Dates, Maps and Sets have no own enumerable keys, so canonicalStringify (revisions.ts lines 131-143) serializes all of them as an empty object. Any change to a Date value or Map/Set contents leaves the hash unchanged. The compiled-content path today feeds JSON-parsed data, but the signature is content: unknown and the beat compiler builds objects in JS where a Date can appear unnoticed.
- toJSON is ignored: an object with a toJSON method hashes by its raw own keys, diverging from JSON.stringify semantics that the doc comment (line 116) claims to match.
- Function-valued keys are NOT omitted: canonicalStringify hits the line-146 fallback, JSON.stringify(fn) returns the value undefined, and the canonical string contains the literal token undefined -- not valid JSON, contradicting both the doc comment ("matching JSON.stringify semantics"; JSON.stringify omits function-valued keys) and the canonical-JSON contract. Why two prior reviews would miss it: every test in tests/revisions.test.ts feeds plain JSON-safe literals; the module reads fluently and the doc comments assert the exact properties the code lacks.

Fix direction: either validate input is JSON-representable (throw with a clear message on NaN/Infinity/BigInt/function/Date/Map/Set/circular) or canonicalize them explicitly. Silence is the bug; either explicit behavior satisfies scenario 1.

### F2 (should-fix) Migration entry validation accepts entries that cannot "link old revision to new"

Spec passage (REQ-CP-05 scenario 2): "a migration map entry exists linking old revision to new."
README contract (content/migrations/README.md): fromRevision/toRevision are "the 16-character hex hash".

- empty-string itemId/fromRevision/toRevision/note: PASSES validation.
- non-hex, wrong-length revisions (not-a-hash!!, ZZZ): PASSES validation.
- fromRevision identical to toRevision (no-op entry): PASSES.
- two entries with the same {itemId, fromRevision} pointing at DIFFERENT toRevisions (fx4, across two files): PASSES, both returned. A downstream consumer resolving an attempt recorded against the old revision now has an ambiguous, unresolvable mapping -- the map no longer links old to new, it forks.

The zod schema (revisions.ts lines 12-17) is four bare z.string() fields. Minimum hardening: nonempty, 16-char lowercase-hex regex for the two revision fields, reject fromRevision === toRevision, and reject duplicate {itemId, fromRevision} pairs across the whole load. The README documents the hex format; the code does not enforce its own README.
